music.brief: Low steady pulse under a soft string pad, calm and focused, one gentle lift near the end, instrumental, for a short explainer video, about 60 seconds.

sources: Potegal & Davidson (2003). Temper Tantrums in Young Children: 2. Tantrum Duration and Temporal Organization. Journal of Developmental & Behavioral Pediatrics. 335 children, 18 to 60 months.

drafted.note: Rewrite of the 2026-10-24 reel as one study told in order: the length, the closer look, the two parts, and the advice that comes out of them.

beats.text: A tantrum has two parts. The second one reaches for you.
beats.say: A tantrum has two parts, and the second one reaches for you.

beats.text: Here is how researchers found them, and what to do in each.
beats.say: Here is how researchers found them, and what to do in each.

beats.text: Parents of 335 children, 18 months to 5 years, wrote down each tantrum.
beats.say: The parents of three hundred thirty five toddlers and preschoolers wrote down each tantrum soon after it ended.

beats.text: The most common tantrum lasted half a minute to a minute.
beats.say: The most common one lasted half a minute to a minute. Three in four were over within five minutes.

beats.text: Then they looked at every half minute.
beats.sub: Two things were happening at once.
beats.say: Then the researchers looked at each half minute, and saw two things happening at once.

beats.text: Part one is anger. It peaks at the start, then falls away.
beats.say: The first part was anger. Screaming and kicking peaked right at the start, then fell away.

beats.text: Part two is sadness. It builds slowly underneath, and lasts longer.
beats.say: Underneath it, sadness built slowly, from whining to crying to reaching for comfort.

beats.text: The honest catch: the times came from parents' accounts.
beats.say: The honest catch is that parents reported these times. Nobody used a stopwatch.

beats.text: In the anger, stay close and quiet. In the sadness, comfort.
beats.sub: When they reach for you, that is your moment.
beats.say: So in the anger, stay close and quiet. When they reach for you, that is your moment to comfort them.

beats.text: See what sits under the next meltdown.
beats.say: Our free tool, What's underneath the meltdown, is in the bio.
